name: Text highlight
description: A way to mark text inside a sentence, for search matches or phrases that need attention. It's subtle by default, with colour variants for warnings, errors, successes and info.

classes.ayy-text-highlight: Inline highlighted span or <mark>: subtle gray wash with clean underline.
classes.ayy-text-highlight--warning: Amber/yellow tint for cautions and warnings.
classes.ayy-text-highlight--destructive: Red tint for errors and danger callouts.
classes.ayy-text-highlight--success: Green tint for positive results or matches.

default.looks: Subtle gray wash with clean underline, inheriting text colour.

hover.none: A text annotation, not a control.

pressed.none: A text annotation, not a control.

disabled.none: A text annotation, not a control.

selected.none: A text annotation, not a control.

error.none: Use variant destructive for error or danger callouts.

js: textHighlightClass({ variant?, className? }) → string; textHighlightParts(text, query) splits text into matching and non-matching segments.

props.text: string — text to search and highlight within (or provide as string children)
props.query: string — search substring or space-separated words to highlight
props.as: ElementType — HTML tag (defaults to mark for callouts, Fragment for queries)

a11y: Uses the standard <mark> HTML tag for search and text highlights, recognised by assistive technology.
Maintains readable contrast across light, dark, and high-contrast themes via color-mix() and light-dark().
Under Windows High Contrast mode (forced-colors), highlights switch to the system Highlight and HighlightText colours.
do: Use TextHighlight to show matched search terms in command palettes, comboboxes, and search results.
Use the default subtle gray highlight with underline for search results so text remains calm and readable.
Use color variants (warning/yellow, destructive/red, success/green, info, orange) for specific semantic callouts.
dont: Don't hardcode background or text colours; use the tokens or built-in variants.
Don't highlight entire paragraphs; highlight only matched keywords or key phrases.
Don't replace links or buttons with highlights.

examples.title: Semantic color variants (yellow, red, green, blue, orange)
